title: Choose the next Third Hour composition
question: All three directions keep the approved espresso, cream, muted-gold, Cormorant, and real-café-photography world. Pick the page structure you want to see developed next—no website code changes are included in this round.

options.label: The Window Table
options.lineage: A quiet café table seen through a warm after-hours window
options.thesis: Arrival comes first: one intimate table setting makes Third Hour feel like a place you can step into.
options.viewport: A lit table and drink image occupies the left two-thirds; a tall serif promise, location cue, and two clear actions stack in a slim cream-edged right column.
options.risk: The most atmospheric option; it needs strong real photography so it never becomes a generic night-café mood board.

options.label: The Night Shift Menu
options.lineage: A café counter menu reorganised as an elegant late-hour service board
options.thesis: The menu is the invitation: a visitor can feel the café’s rhythm and choose their first drink immediately.
options.viewport: A wide, numbered drink list holds the left side while one oversized drink portrait breaks the grid on the right; story and loyalty sit as compact service notes below the primary order cue.
options.risk: The clearest menu-led option; the structural grid must stay editorial rather than reading like a food-delivery app.

options.label: The Stampbook Society
options.lineage: A personal café stampbook opened on a table, with collected moments tucked inside
options.thesis: Third Hour becomes a ritual worth returning to by making coffee, food, and the loyalty card feel like one keepsake.
options.viewport: A large opened stampbook fills the center; on one page is the café promise and drink image, on the other is a ten-stamp card and a direct loyalty invitation, with discovery links around its edges.
options.risk: The most memorable loyalty bridge; it must preserve café discovery as the lead rather than making the public site feel like an account dashboard.
